Consolidated summaries tend to shed caveats and sample limits, and a claim that broad from a single SMB pricing test is exactly the shape of an over-generalized memory. Discount-led acquisition is also the classic case where a short-window revenue win conceals worse retention and lower-quality accounts, i.e. it can raise booked revenue while lowering *sustainable qualified* revenue. So I spend one verification pull on memory_73 to see the original record's segment, horizon, and whether retention was actually measured or merely not observed.

Second pull is memory_31, because it is the mechanism I intend to act on and it carries its own downstream value risk: 'cutting required fields at signup' improves activation partly by admitting less-qualified signups and by destroying the qualification data sales needs. That trades measured funnel lift against unmeasured pipeline quality. memory_44 is consistent with this worry, since enterprise pipeline quality depends on the richer sales-assisted path. I am not treating memory as false, only as compressed.
